findings.reason: The initial proposal path now publishes its validated temporary file with an atomic no-replace link when the store was absent. The saved interleaving regression observes a successful v1 migration before proposal publication and verifies that proposal refuses while the migrated bytes survive unchanged.

Descriptor reads now include O_NONBLOCK and reject every non-regular fstat result before reading. The real FIFO subprocess regression returns the typed CLI refusal within its two-second bound instead of waiting for a writer.
Whole-store parsing now rejects a repeated memory_id before a mutation callback can append or write. The regression preserves the duplicate store byte-for-byte.
Final record UTF-8 serialization now converts invalid Unicode metadata into MemoryMigrationError. The guarded-store regression verifies the CLI-facing mutation leaves the malformed bytes unchanged.
Proposal normalizes the workspace identity once before binding both workspace_id and source scope, matching the existing recall comparison. The padded-id regression observes project-a in both fields.

The interrupted full-diff reviewer reproduced a second invalid-Unicode path: content hashing raised UnicodeEncodeError before final serialization. parse_v2_record now translates that root cause to MemoryMigrationError, and the new red/green case preserves the malformed store unchanged.

docs/formats.md previously listed the earlier v2 mutation commands without propose. The docs-only maintenance follow-up updated the format inventory and was merged in PR #57 as ca58517d7f2e1b2e42ba456bc9de3f0d7073fa87; this record closes the deferred finding against that readback.

The fixed-SHA reviewer demonstrated that migration exposed an empty final target before writing, allowing proposal replacement while both commands reported success. Migration now stages the target as owner-write-only, writes and fsyncs the complete payload, then makes it readable; every v2 read/proposal refuses an unreadable regular target as incomplete. A real cross-process regression pauses migration at the visible target and proves proposal refuses until migration publishes the intact legacy record; the opposite interleave remains protected by proposal no-replace publication.

The post-cap new-diff review demonstrated that fchmod(0644) would widen a store created under umask 077 from the previous 0600 result to world-readable 0644. Completed migration publication now becomes owner-only 0600, matching proposal-store privacy, and a real permissions regression verifies the final mode plus readable record.
